speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having a pruritic rash, fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; to better understand your condition, please describe when these symptoms started and if they are worsening. Have you had any recent contact with sick individuals or been in a crowded place?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Measles (Rubeola).

The clinical presentation of an initial fever and respiratory prodrome followed by a pruritic rash that appeared 4 days later and specifically spares the perioral area is classic for Measles. I am confident in this diagnosis based on the provided history.
